content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. While using this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as liver function tests, fibrinogen levels, blood counts, or cultures, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, it is important to take the medication as soon as possible according to the prescribed schedule. For storage instructions, consult the product guidelines or your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. Please note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about this medication. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Before using tigecycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other tetracyclines (such as doxycycline, minocycline, or tetracycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Tigecycline may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. Tigecycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, this medication can increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Children under the age of 8 may be more susceptible to side effects, particularly tooth discoloration, which has also been observed in older children and young adults. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using tigecycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist.
